root_cause.text: Missing cleanup calls to `ksmbd_vfs_kern_path_end_removing()` on error paths after `ksmbd_vfs_kern_path_start_removing()` acquires inode locks and references, causing unbalanced lock acquisition and resource leaks.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows that two error paths (lines with `goto out;` inside the `if (rc)` and `else` blocks) were exiting without calling the corresponding cleanup function `ksmbd_vfs_kern_path_end_removing()`. The fix moves the cleanup call outside the conditional blocks and adds a conditional check to only `goto out;` after cleanup is performed. The CVE description explicitly states "There are two places where ksmbd_vfs_kern_path_end_removing() needs to be called in order to balance what the corresponding successful call to ksmbd_vfs_kern_path_start_removing() has done, i.e. drop inode locks and put the taken references," and the kernel warning shows "2 locks held by kworker" that were never released due to missing cleanup on error paths.

intent_record.intent_summary: Ensure ksmbd_vfs_kern_path_end_removing() is always called before error exit to prevent resource leaks in smb2_create_link error paths.
intent_record.what: Removed two `goto out;` statements from within conditional blocks (lines 6118 and 6122) and added a single consolidated `if (rc) goto out;` check after the `ksmbd_vfs_kern_path_end_removing(&path);` call.
intent_record.how: This change defers the error handling exit until after path cleanup is performed. Previously, errors would immediately jump to the cleanup label, potentially skipping the `ksmbd_vfs_kern_path_end_removing(&path)` call. Now the function always executes path cleanup before checking if an error occurred and exiting, ensuring proper resource management regardless of which error condition is triggered.

This prevents the unbalanced lock acquisition and resource leaks that occur when ksmbd_vfs_kern_path_start_removing() acquires inode locks and references but the corresponding cleanup function is not called on error exit.
